name: Tibero
tagline: Korean Oracle-compatible RDBMS with RAC-style Active Cluster, popular for Oracle exits in Asia.
description: Tibero is a commercial relational database from TmaxTibero (spun out of TmaxSoft) whose selling point is high compatibility with Oracle Database: PL/SQL-style procedures, Oracle SQL syntax and data types, and Tibero Active Cluster (TAC), a shared-disk cluster modelled on Oracle RAC. That makes it a common target in Korean public sector and financial institutions that want to leave Oracle without rewriting applications. The Tibero 7.2 line is actively patched (PatchSet04 in October 2025 added columnar compression) and an AI-focused Tibero 8 is in development. Outside Korea and parts of Asia, support and talent are thin.

pricing.notes: Commercial licences typically priced well below Oracle Enterprise Edition; a demo licence is available for evaluation.

scale.notes: TAC shared-disk clustering for scale-out and HA; standby databases for DR.

strengths: High Oracle SQL and PL/SQL compatibility reduces application rewrites on migration
Tibero Active Cluster offers RAC-like shared-disk HA at lower cost
Strong presence and local support in Korean government and finance
Columnar compression (TCC) added in the 7.2 line for storage savings
weaknesses: Small ecosystem and documentation outside Korea
Compatibility with Oracle is high but not complete; testing is still required
No vector search or modern multi-model features yet
useCases: Replacing Oracle Database in public-sector systems
Banking and insurance core systems in Korea
Lowering licence cost for Oracle-style applications
notIdealFor: Teams outside Asia without local vendor support
